key_concepts: A microscope magnifies objects too small for the naked eye
Microscopy is the science of investigating small objects and structures
The compound microscope was invented around 1590 by Dutch spectacle makers
Robert Hooke coined the term cell after observing cork
Anton van Leeuwenhoek was the first to observe bacteria
The eyepiece and objective lenses magnify the specimen
Total magnification is eyepiece magnification multiplied by objective magnification
The diaphragm regulates light passing through the specimen
Coarse and fine adjustment knobs focus the image
The stage and stage clips hold the slide in place
Proper handling includes carrying the microscope by the arm and base
Oil immersion objectives are used to view bacteria and very small protists
